chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Our Shia are the people of guidance, and the people of piety, and the people of goodness, and the people of faith, and the people of victory and triumph.
ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of the Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the Shia not merely by lineage but by their embodiment of *al-huda* (divine guidance) and *al-tuqa* (piety), establishing them as the true heirs of prophetic wisdom. This description underscores the theological concept of *al-ghalaba* (victory) for the faithful, linking their spiritual integrity to ultimate success in both this world and the hereafter, a key theme in Shia eschatology.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ourasws Shia are the people of guidance, and the people of piety, and the people of goodness, and the people of Emān, and people of victory and triumph’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Our Shi’a (followers) are people of guidance, of piety, of goodness, of belief and people of victory and triumph.”
